title: Closures with Multiple Parameters
hints: Operators such as `+` and functions such as `max` can be passed as closures.
`zip(a, b).map(f)` feeds each `(x, y)` pair into a two-argument function.
For power: `(0..<exponent).reduce(1) { acc, _ in acc * base }`.
jsBridge: Operators are functions in Swift, so you can pass `+` or `max` directly as a `(Int, Int) -> Int` closure: `zipWith(a, b, +)`. In JS you'd write `(x, y) => x + y`, because `+` isn't a value.

compass.q: JS can't pass `+` as a function. What does it mean that Swift operators are just functions?
Why does passing `max` sometimes need a type annotation (overload ambiguity)?
`zip(a, b).map(+)`: does that work? Why or why not (tuple splat)?
Where would a higher-order `zipWith` show up in UI code: chart series, diffing?
